description: We are a team that met in the UGR LDU challenge
summary:
We are living through a new era of space exploration. Discovering what lies beyond our planet has never mattered more, which makes it essential to assess the viability of lunar missions.
OSSM offers an easy, intuitive, and fast way to check at a glance whether a lunar mission is viable. It evaluates landing feasibility on the selected terrain, checks whether Earth is visible from the site, and considers both topography and the Sun’s position to determine natural light availability.
For the analysis, we propose several sample landings, both at the Apollo 11 landing site and at locations near the lunar south pole, which are of interest because of their complex topography.
details:
OSSM is an interactive, visual tool for assessing the viability of lunar expeditions. Its interface lets users choose different points on the Moon to evaluate for landing. After a site is selected, an interactive 3D model of the Earth, the Sun, and the Moon lets users set the mission parameters (landing date and time). Once the parameters are set, a simulation runs and an animation shows intuitively which criteria have failed. OSSM also reports the specific values behind each failure; for example, if the terrain is unstable, it shows the measured slope.

A site is viable only if it meets all of the following criteria (the default values can be changed):

  1. Terrain slope: the 95th percentile (P95) of the slope must be below 15°.
  2. Valid data: the input data must be complete, valid and consistent with the site.
  3. Unobstructed Sun at start: neither the terrain nor an eclipse may block the Sun at the initial instant.
  4. Earth visible at start: Earth must be above the terrain horizon at the initial instant.
  5. Solar elevation at start: the Sun must be more than 5° above the horizon.
  6. Accumulated light: the hours of light must exceed 50% of the mission hours.
  7. Time coverage: the data series must cover the whole requested duration.

OSSM is built with TypeScript, Three.js, and CSS for the interface, the 3D visualization, and the animations, and with Python for the scientific computation. The video was created using CapCut.

Our goal is to make the viability check accessible to users of different levels, both technical and non-technical. For non-technical users, OSSM also works as a teaching tool: the interactive 3D model and the animated explanation of each failure turn abstract mission constraints into an entertaining, intuitive experience for students of all levels.
